text.p: Turkish central bank stepped in the money and bond markets on Wednesday to ease a 84.8 trillion lira cash shortage caused by banks' 155.4 trillion lira of auction payments to the treasury, bankers said.

The bank lent 19.9 trillion lira at 72 percent overnight and 11.7 trillion at 70 percent via tomorrow/next deals on the money interbank. It injected 31 trillion lira via a seven-day repo auction at 74 percent on the open market at midday.
The average overnight repo rate rose sharply to 76.04 percent from 68.40 on Tuesday and the average overnight money rate jumped to 71.74 percent from previous 53.76.
The central bank said it also stepped in the bond market after the repo auction to lend cash to banks through o/n repos at 80 percent and seven day repos at 75.20 percent.
Bankers said the market opened extremely short after the Treasury's unexpectedly high nine-month t-bill auction sale on Tuesday at sharply higher levels.
The treasury met all of the bids by selling 290.2 trillion lira worth of nine-month t-bills on Tuesday, sharply raising the yield to 106.69 percent.
